## This manuscript's history

This version revises the expanded OpenAI manuscript after Claude's second review rejected it as a finalist. Claude's review proposed investigating the symmetric score family and supplied a betting example. This revision proves the family's shrinking/preservation/extremizing classification, generalizes and checks the betting calculation, and examines the difference between fixed-prior idempotence and sequential reuse. It reframes the contribution around choosing a learning standard. The new version has not itself been independently reviewed.

The original general proper-loss equalizer and boosting characterization are retained. The probability-scale scores and weight-function construction are credited as established. The 5,391-word manuscript passed the word limit and basic manuscript scan. New targeted checks cover 56 score/prior cases and 81 exact rational betting cases. These do not settle philosophical importance or novelty.

The human requested AI-generated philosophical essays, supplied or retrieved primary texts, set resource and length constraints, asked for stronger arguments and literature checks, and arranged comparisons between model outputs. The recorded workflow instructions also requested adversarial review and subsequent revision. The human stated that philosophical feedback was being withheld for the contest. The available record does not replace a complete audit of every earlier exchange.

The inspected corpus contains ten developed manuscript tracks and eight exploratory drafts. Three developed OpenAI manuscripts rework the three original Claude projects; the tracks are therefore not all independent topics. These counts measure candidates and artifacts, not established discoveries. Revisions, blind-review copies, and a later A6 research note are not counted as additional essays.

The present preparation set is provisional. A current-version referee result could change which manuscripts are selected. No contest entry was submitted during this revision pass.

## Sources, evaluation, and tools

The authoring workflows used supplied documents, repository source extracts, and web retrieval for literature comparison and citation checks. The argument-agnostic scaffold required explicit claims, strong objections, source fidelity, and a distinction between novelty and correctness. The project used synthetic AI referee perspectives. These are not reviews endorsed by the philosophers whose research informed a perspective.

Validation distinguishes hand proofs, exact examples, finite enumeration, numerical checks, and source-reading boundaries. This revised manuscript counts 5,391 words under the repository strict counter, excluding its reference section and including title, headings, abstract, mathematical tokens, and footnotes. Its basic manuscript scan returned no hard flags. These checks do not establish originality, philosophical importance, or completeness of citation verification.
